root_cause.text: In KVM nSVM, nested_sync_control_from_vmcb02() failed to copy the CPU-updated int_state/interrupt-shadow bit from vmcb02 into the cached vmcb12 authoritative nested-state structure, causing stale nested state and restoration of the interrupt shadow to the wrong VMCB.
root_cause.evidence: The patch adds `svm->nested.ctl.int_state = svm->vmcb->control.int_state;` to `nested_sync_control_from_vmcb02()`, and the CVE/commit message explicitly states that `int_state` “is also written by the CPU ... but it is not sync'd to cached vmcb12,” which could restore interrupt shadow into `vmcb01` instead of `vmcb02` and hang L2.

intent_record.intent_summary: Synchronize int_state from vmcb02 into nested control state so nested virtualization preserves the current interrupt state correctly.
intent_record.what: A new assignment was added in nested_sync_control_from_vmcb02() to copy svm->vmcb->control.int_state into svm->nested.ctl.int_state, alongside the existing synchronization of event_inj and event_inj_err.
intent_record.how: This makes the nested control state preserve and propagate the interrupt state from vmcb02 into the nested cached control structure, preventing int_state from being left stale or unsynchronized during nested virtualization state syncing.

grouping_result.intent: Synchronize int_state from vmcb02 into nested control state so nested virtualization preserves the current interrupt state correctly.

relevance_review.reason: The group directly addresses the root cause by syncing the CPU-updated int_state/interrupt-shadow from vmcb02 into the authoritative nested control state, preventing stale nested state and incorrect interrupt shadow restoration.

candidates.rationale: This function was synchronizing selected CPU-updated control state from vmcb02 into the authoritative nested control cache, but it omitted syncing int_state. The nearby explicit sync of event injection fields highlights the incomplete state propagation that caused stale nested interrupt-shadow state.

By limiting synchronization of processor-written interrupt control state to only V_IRQ and V_TPR bits, the code excluded the CPU-updated int_state/interrupt-shadow bit, directly causing vmcb12's cached nested state to become stale.

vuln_statements.explanation: This statement defines the set of interrupt-control bits synchronized from vmcb02 into the authoritative nested control cache. By including only V_IRQ_MASK and V_TPR_MASK, it omitted the CPU-updated int_state/interrupt-shadow bit, which is the root cause of the stale nested state and incorrect restoration behavior.

bic_trace_step.commit_msg:
KVM: nSVM: synchronize VMCB controls updated by the processor on every vmexit

The control state changes on every L2->L0
bic_trace_step.code_snippet:
commit 2d8a42be0e2b15a4e0b20349f27bb8288db5ebe6
Author: Paolo Bonzini <pbonzini@redhat.com>
Date:   Fri May 22 03:50:14 2020 -0400

    KVM: nSVM: synchronize VMCB controls updated by the processor on every vmexit
    
    The control state changes on every L2->L0 vmexit, and we will have to
    serialize it in the nested state.  So keep it up to date in svm->nested.ctl
    and just copy them back to the nested VMCB in nested_svm_vmexit.
    
    Signed-off-by: Paolo Bonzini <pbonzini@redhat.com
bic_trace_step.reason: The provided diff is sufficient because it shows the exact synchronization helper added by this commit and how nested_svm_vmexit() now sources fields from svm->nested.ctl. The root cause is failure to copy the CPU-updated int_state/interrupt-shadow bit from vmcb02 into the authoritative cached nested state. In this commit, the new helper `sync_nested_vmcb_control(struct vcpu_svm *svm)` synchronizes only `event_inj`, `event_inj_err`, and selected bits of `int_ctl` (`mask = V_IRQ_MASK | V_TPR_MASK; ... svm->nested.ctl.int_ctl |= svm->vmcb->control.int_ctl & mask;`). It does not copy `int_state` at all. Also, in `nested_svm_vmexit()`, `nested_vmcb->control.int_state = vmcb->control.int_state;` still copies directly from `vmcb` rather than via cached authoritative nested state, while `int_ctl`, `tlb_ctl`, `event_inj`, and `event_inj_err` are taken from `svm->nested.ctl`. Therefore, the specific vulnerable construct described in the root cause—failing to synchronize CPU-updated `int_state` / interrupt shadow into the cached nested control state—is absent from this function body as shown, so `has_bug` is false for the provided code snippet. At the same time, the fix for the described bug is also not present, because there is no synchronization of `int_state` into `svm->nested.ctl` or equivalent authoritative nested-state cache.
